item.title: Dr. Athanasopoulos Virtual Lecture - Un Desvio Pa Porta De Sol (Sponsored by the Puerto Rican Independence Party)
item.description: Please join Dr. Athanasopoulos and the Puerto Rican Independence Party (PIP) at his upcoming virtual lecture on September 26th, 2025, 6PM-7:30PM ET. This talk is part of PIP's week-long commemoration of El Grito De Lares (The Cry of Lares) which was the first major push for Puerto Rican Independence against the Spanish Empire pre-US colonization in 1898. Description below & flyers (in English & Spanish attached). If you cannot attend, please consider sharing with folks who may be interested.

item.title: Black Iconoclasm by Dr. Charles Athanasopoulos Wins the 2025 Critical and Cultural Studies Division Book of the Year Award!
item.description: AAAS Assistant Professor, Dr. Charles Athanasopoulos book, Black Iconoclasm, was recently awarded the 2025 Critical and Cultural Studies Division Book of the Year Award by the National Communication Association. This is the second major award following the 2025 First Book Prize awarded by the Cultural Studies Association.

item.title: NBC 4 Publish Article on Celebrating the Arts and Humanities
item.description: Congratulation AAAS Professor Ryan Skinner on your essay celebrating the importance of the Arts and Humanities being published by NBC! item.title: Congratulations Dr. Pranav Jani on Launching Your New Podcast Called Together We Rise!
item.description: “Together We Rise: Solidarity Stories from Central Ohio" features interviews with organizers and activists Dr. Pranav Jani has worked with for 20+ years in Columbus. Many are connected with OSU. Here the link to podcast pranavjani.com/togetherwerise!

item.title: Congratulations, AAAS Interim Chair Sunnie Rucker-Chang on Your Recent Journal Publication in Slavic Review, "Critical Forum: Blackness in Slavic, East European, and Eurasian Societies."
item.description: Congratulations Dr. Sunnie Rucker-Chang on your publication in a special issue of Slavic Review: Critical Forum: Blackness in Slavic, East European, and Eurasian Societies. This special issue is co-edited with Nana Osei-Opare (Rice University).

item.title: Congratulations Dr. View on Your Upcoming Publication "Curriculum of the Mind"!
item.description: Stevie “Dr. View” Johnson is an award-winning DJ, producer, scholar, and cultural architect whose work sits at the intersection of Black sound, creative practice, community organizing, and critical scholarship. He currently serves as the Assistant Professor of Creative Practice in Popular Music at The Ohio State University, where he advances a model of Hip Hop creative practice that integrates DJing, sampling, mashups, cultural memory, and community-based research. item.title: Congratulations Dr. Maxamed Abu-maye on the Publication of "Follow the Rain" in the Journal of Black Studies & Research!
item.description: The article titled "Follow the Rain: Freedom Summer 2020 and Somali American Political Consciousness,” is published with The Black Scholar: Journal of Black Studies and Research. The authors—Muna-Udbi A. Ali, Maxamed Abumaye, and Jessie Mills—explore the emergence of Somali American political consciousness and activism within the Black Lives Matter movement, particularly during the summer of 2020.

item.title: Congratulations, University Senator, Dr. Michael R. Fisher Jr!
item.description: Congratulation Dr. Michael R. Fisher Jr. on being appointed to a three-year term as a senator representing the Division of Arts & Humanities! Dr. Fishers term runs from Fall Semester, 2026 through Spring Semester of 2029. Hooray!
